CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE R. NATARAJ  ORAL ORDER

The petitioner has called in question the charge sheet filed against him in C.C. No.51150/2018 (arising out of Crime No.453/2016 registered by the respondent No.1 - Police) pending on the file of the X Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Mayohall Unit, Bengaluru, for the offence punishable under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short, 'IPC').
NC: 2026:KHC:12965 HC-KAR 2.

entities.text: X Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Mayohall Unit, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The petitioner is the husband of the respondent No.2.

Due to certain differences between them,
the respondent No.2 informed the respondent No.1 on 21.07.2016 that the petitioner and his mother were demanding money to purchase a house.
She alleged that when her mother tried to convince the petitioner and his mother, they abused her and her mother.

Later, the respondent No.2 was forced Sri Danty Yerra vs State Of Karnataka on 3 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142518990/
2 to seek Police assistance and then the Police arrived at the scene and summoned all of them to the Station.

entities.text: Sri Danty Yerra vs State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the same day, after they returned back from the police station, the petitioner's mother and his brother- in-law/Mr. Jomy Jose beat up the respondent No.2.

Later, the respondent No.2 was thrown out of the matrimonial home on 19.07.2016. at 10.30 p.m.
3.

Based on the above complaint, the respondent No.1 registered Crime No.453/2016 for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 504 read with Section 34 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 against the petitioner, his mother and brother-in-law.
After investigation, the charge sheet was filed against the petitioner for the offence punishable under Section 498A of the IPC.
However, the names of the mother and brother-in-law of the petitioner were NC: 2026:KHC:12965 HC-KAR dropped from the charge sheet.
Being aggrieved by the said charge sheet filed against him, the petitioner is before this Court.

4. The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the respondent No.1 - Police without counselling the parties as directed by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar and Another [AIR 2014 SC 2756] has straightaway registered an F.I.R.

entities.text: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar and Another [AIR 2014 SC 2756]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He also contends that the averments made in the complaint if read as a whole, are not sufficient to attract an offence under Section 498 of IPC.

5. The learned High Court Government Pleader appearing for respondent No.1 submitted that a perusal of the complaint shows that the respondent No.2 was harassed for dowry by the petitioner and his mother that she was thrown out of the matrimonial home on 19.07.2016.

He also contends that the respondent No.2 lodged a complaint on 21.07.2016, which was investigated and a charge sheet was filed against the petitioner for an offence punishable under Section 498A of IPC.
NC: 2026:KHC:12965 HC-KAR 6.
I have considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1.

The respondent No. 2 though served with notice,
has not entered appearance before this Court.

7. The respondent No.2 alleged that the petitioner and his mother demanded dowry from her to purchase a house and when the respondent No.2 refused, the petitioner and his mother ganged up and assaulted the respondent No.2 and abused her mother.
It is also alleged that the respondent No.2 was thrown out of the matrimonial home on 19.07.2016.
The respondent No.2 is an educated lady.
She has not disclosed as to what prevented her from filing a complaint before the respondent No.1 - Police on 19.07.2016 or from lodging a complaint immediately thereafter or at least the next day.
However, the complaint was lodged on 21.07.2016 and there is no reason forthcoming for the delay in lodging the complaint.
The accusations made in the complaint also do not constitute an offence under Section 498A of IPC, as there is no serious threat to life or limb of the respondent No.2.

In that view of the matter, this Court is of the opinion that an offence under NC:
2026:KHC:12965 HC-KAR Section 498A of IPC was not made out, and hence the registration of an FIR against the petitioner was wholly unwarranted.
